solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Opposes detective breaking agreements

indicators.note: the detective breaks into the agreements, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A police officer is wrecking a set of deals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' suggests a detective breaking a case or breaking the law; here it only means entering. DI is the usual British police rank abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict a claim is to oppose it by asserting the reverse, a plain synonym in the argumentative sense.

clue.text: Ruined castle — contest message of acceptance?

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of the following word are thrown into disorder

parts.note: to vie is to compete, to contest

explanation.surface: A ruined castle is the prize in a contest, and someone shrugs it off.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase is used in English to shrug off misfortune.
explanation.definitionFit: C'est la vie is French for 'that's life', a phrase of resigned acceptance.

clue.text: Snooper interrupted more than once by one more vociferous

indicators.note: being interrupted by a letter means having it break into the word
the interruption happens twice, so a second copy goes in

parts.note: a noser is one who noses about, a snooper
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A busybody keeps being cut off by someone louder.
explanation.walkthrough: The snooper is one who noses about; a single I breaks into it in two places, once after the O and once after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone vociferous is loud and clamorous, so being more vociferous means making more noise.

clue.text: Function of lowly commoner, not leader

indicators.note: the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a prole is a member of the working class

explanation.surface: Asking what purpose an ordinary worker serves once the boss is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Prole is short for proletarian, from Orwell's 1984.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the part something plays, as in 'the role of the heart', is its function.

clue.text: One in a sort of tree but not atop it

definitions.text: One in a sort of tree
definitions.meaning: reads as a bird or climber in the branches; the setter means a name on a family tree
reads as low in the branches; the setter means anyone below the founding ancestor

explanation.surface: Something perched in a tree, but lower than the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'sort of tree' is a family tree, where descendants appear below their ancestors; the answer also hints at climbing down.
explanation.definitionFit: On a family tree the ancestors sit at the top and every later generation hangs below them, so the whole clue describes a descendant.

clue.text: Smart attempt to capture a city

indicators.note: smart and attempt together take the A captive between them

parts.note: have a go = make an attempt

explanation.surface: A slick bid to take over a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capture a city' reads as a military aim, but the city is the definition and A is what gets captured.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Chicago is one particular city, the largest in Illinois.

clue.text: Head of sailing to pick member of crew

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to cull is to select or pick out

explanation.surface: The chief of a sailing club chooses someone for the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The rowing sense sits in plain sight; the S comes from sailing, not from any sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A scull is an oar, and by extension a sculler rowing with one, so a member of a rowing crew.

clue.text: Islamic ruler sacrificing one young animal

indicators.note: the ruler gives up one of his letters

parts.note: calif is a spelling of caliph

explanation.surface: A ruler offers up a young beast in sacrifice.
explanation.walkthrough: The common spelling caliph would not work; the variant CALIF loses its I.
explanation.definitionFit: A general term for a specific case: calves are the young of cattle, and also of whales and elephants.

clue.text: Lecturer is into cannabis, endlessly looking for kicks?

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the lecturer and is are put within the shortened cannabis
endlessly means without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A university lecturer takes to cannabis, endlessly seeking thrills.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase describing an activity; hedonism is the noun for that pleasure-seeking pursuit, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonism is the pursuit of pleasure, the life of someone always seeking thrills.

clue.text: Player's very short attack

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to assail is to attack; drop the L

explanation.surface: A sportsman makes a very brief raid.
explanation.walkthrough: The player is a musician: assai is the Italian score marking for 'very', as in allegro assai. 'Very' looks like the intensifier for 'short'.
explanation.definitionFit: In musical directions, assai means very.

clue.text: Lethargy — it is evident in girl of the upper classes half dead

indicators.note: IT shows up alongside the girl
only half of the word is used

parts.note: U = upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A posh girl so listless she looks half dead.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were terms for upper-class and other British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name a heavy, sluggish want of energy.

clue.text: Lift female unwell with minimal cash

parts.note: 1p, one penny, the smallest British coin, written as IP

explanation.surface: Hoisting a sick woman who has hardly any money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' reads as a verb about hoisting, but it is a boost to morale. The digit 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift in its noun sense, a boost to spirits, as in 'the news gave us a lift'.

clue.text: Abandoned gaol is accommodating former monarch's wives and mistresses

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so the shuffled letters hold the royal initials
abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters of gaol is run loose

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of the late Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A disused prison now houses a dead king's harem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned gaol' looks like a derelict prison, but 'Abandoned' is the signal to rearrange, and 'is' joins the fodder rather than linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the women's quarters of an Ottoman palace, and by extension the harem of wives and concubines kept there.

clue.text: An opening accordingly accommodates a new garden plant

explanation.surface: A gap is made for putting in a new plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted A N sits at the join between A GAP and THUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The agapanthus, or African lily, is a popular garden plant.

clue.text: Learner always "getting on" financed by loans

explanation.surface: A trainee forever borrowing to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks point to the idiom: someone getting on is old.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveraged purchase is funded with borrowed money.

clue.text: Girl is fitted into space module that allows no room for flexibility

definitions.text: that allows no room for flexibility

indicators.note: fitted into means placed inside, so the girl and is go within the module

parts.note: LEM is the Lunar Excursion Module of the Apollo missions
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl is squeezed into a cramped space capsule with no spare room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No room' fits the cramped capsule, but the definition is about rigid rules, not space.
explanation.definitionFit: Legalism is strict adherence to the letter of the law, a rigid outlook with no flexibility.

clue.text: Look, a pig somewhat larger than this animal

indicators.note: the phrase is a little bigger than the answer, which sits inside it

parts.note: the letters run from the end of Look through to the start of pig

explanation.surface: Pointing out a pig that is a bit bigger than some other beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat larger than' seems to compare animal sizes; it says the words 'look a pig' are slightly longer than the answer hidden in them.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest animal related to the giraffe.

clue.text: A new silo for storing what is harvested — impressive building

indicators.note: the reshaped letters are for storing, holding inside, the harvest
new means made afresh, so the letters of a silo are formed into a new order

parts.note: a crop is what is harvested from the fields

explanation.surface: A farmer's new silo is built to store the harvest, and quite a building it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The farm picture of a silo storing grain is the disguise: 'A' joins 'silo' as fodder, and the harvest sits just inside the rearranged letters, after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acropolis of Athens is the citadel crowned by the Parthenon, the most famous ancient monument in Greece.

clue.text: Form rough judgement of people at party wasting time

explanation.surface: Sizing up partygoers who are frittering the evening away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasting time' reads as idling at the party; it is the instruction to lose T.
explanation.definitionFit: A guess is an estimate made without full evidence, so a plain synonym for judging roughly.

clue.text: Fantastic tail-ender for county dismissed for a half-century

indicators.note: in cricket a tail-ender bats last, so here it picks the last letter of the county
the batsman is dismissed and something else comes in for him, taking his place

parts.note: Surrey is an English county just south-west of London, with a famous cricket side
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, half a century

explanation.surface: A cricket report: Surrey's last batsman was out after scoring fifty, which seemed unreal.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words all point at a scorecard; a tail-ender is the last batsman in, so it is the county's last letter that goes out, replaced by A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal means bizarre and dreamlike, the way fantastic can describe something wildly strange.

clue.text: Star writer with silver-lined vehicle

indicators.note: the vehicle is lined with silver inside it

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A celebrity author with a luxurious car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star writer' looks like a famous author; star is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific case of the general word: the five-pointed figure drawn in one line is a kind of star.

clue.text: Sailor, an isolated marine inhabitant

explanation.surface: A lonely seafarer living out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine' suggests a soldier at sea, but it just means of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the abalone, an edible shellfish, lives on rocky seabeds.

clue.text: Desire to appear with band in silky fabric

indicators.note: the band appears alongside the desire

explanation.surface: Longing to take the stage with one's group dressed in silk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' reads as musicians, but it is a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the word comes from the lustre of this glossy dress silk.

clue.text: Good person leading a very loud workforce

indicators.note: the good person comes first

parts.note: ff = fortissimo, very loud in music

explanation.surface: A decent boss in charge of a noisy crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' reads as managing the workers; it only puts ST first.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the people employed by an organisation.

clue.text: Drink knocked back by river where students live and work

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

indicators.note: knocked back means turned backwards here, as well as hinting at drinking

explanation.surface: Students down drinks by the river near their college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking, but it signals SUP reversed to PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds of a university, where students are housed and study.

clue.text: A party's served up fizzy drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' turns the letters bottom to top

explanation.surface: Pop being handed out at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: A do is a party, so the possessive gives DO'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: soda water, or any carbonated soft drink in American use.

clue.text: Propaganda something wicked? Must keep quiet

indicators.note: the wicked thing must hold quiet inside it

explanation.surface: Is misleading publicity evil? Keep it hushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep quiet' reads as a call for silence, but it tells SIN to hold P.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin is slanted presentation of news, a kind of propaganda.

clue.text: Areas in very fast vehicle out of this world

definitions.text: very fast vehicle out of this world

explanation.surface: Parts of a speedy car that are simply amazing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word placing areas inside something; it is HIP, fashionable. 'Out of this world' is literal for a spaceship.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceship is a very fast vehicle that travels beyond Earth.

clue.text: Presumably rendered able to move round, this writer took initiative

parts.note: to lead is to take the initiative

explanation.surface: The setter got things moving by taking charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presumably' admits that oiling a stiff hinge does not guarantee it moves. 'Move round' is a trap: round belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something oiled has been lubricated so it can move freely.

clue.text: Performing artists get digitally immersed, as Spooner might roughly say?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words; roughly admits the result is only an approximate sound

parts.note: to soak is to immerse in liquid
digits are fingers, so being digitally immersed means the fingers are soaked

explanation.surface: Someone dips their fingers in water, and a Spooner-style slip gives musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get digitally immersed' is SOAK FINGERS; swapping the opening sounds gives roughly FOAK SINGERS, heard as FOLK SINGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Folk singers are musicians who perform traditional songs, so they are performing artists.
